For missing or weak citations on scanned PDFs, support should:

1. Check the upload metadata to confirm whether the file is an image-only PDF and whether the customer’s workspace has OCR enabled; scanned PDFs require OCR to extract text and generate citations [NL-006#NL-006-S03].
2. Inspect the OCR logs to see whether page boundaries were missed during indexing [NL-006#NL-006-S04], and verify that OCR completed without errors [NL-028#NL-028-S03].
3. Ask the customer to inspect scan quality. If possible, they should export the document from the source system as a digital, text-searchable PDF rather than scanning a printed sheet [NL-006#NL-006-S03][NL-028#NL-028-S03].
4. If scanned files must be used, recommend the Advanced OCR Pipeline, available to Enterprise customers or as a Growth add-on, which uses layout-aware vision models to reconstruct text [NL-006#NL-006-S03].
5. Rule out other common causes of missing citations by checking the admin logs for the retrieved source/section ID, verifying the source document is not marked `deprecated` or `stale`, and confirming the user has permission to view the underlying document [NL-006#NL-006-S04].
6. If the PDF layout is complex, advise simplifying the layout (removing sidebars and floating elements) and re-uploading with linear, top-to-bottom text flow [NL-006#NL-006-S04].
7. If tables are garbled, suggest converting the table to `.csv` or `.xlsx` and uploading it separately, or formatting table cells with clear, dark grid lines [NL-006#NL-006-S03].
8. Remind customers that handwritten notes and physical annotations are ignored by the standard OCR engine and must be transcribed into digital text in a DOCX or Markdown file before upload if they need to be searchable [NL-006#NL-006-S03].
9. If a document was re-uploaded, wait for the re-indexing job to show “Success,” clear the tenant’s retrieval cache, and re-run the query to verify citation alignment [NL-006#NL-006-S04].
